title: Krimml Waterfalls
name: Krimml Waterfalls
kurzbeschreibung: The Krimmler Wasserfälle at the Gerlospass: with a 380 m drop the highest waterfalls in Europe, spectacular waterfall trail, and certified healing power.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Krimmler Wasserfälle are situated at the foot of the Gerlospass on the border between Tyrol and the Salzburg Pinzgau in the Nationalpark Hohe Tauern at an altitude between 1,070 and 1,470 metres above sea level. With a breathtaking total drop of 380 metres across three mighty cascade tiers, these roaring falls are the highest waterfalls in Europe and the fifth highest on Earth. Fed by the vast glacial fields of the Venedigergruppe, up to 10,000 litres of ice-cold meltwater from the Krimmler Ache plunge per second over giant granite ledges into the valley basin.

Route & Requirements

This world-famous natural monument was made accessible as early as 1900 by the Österreichischer Alpenverein with the boldly engineered Krimmler Wasserfallweg: a roughly four-kilometre-long trail with switchbacks leads hikers in about 1.5 hours of walking directly alongside the thundering spray from the lowest to the highest fall tier. Spectacular viewing platforms allow captivating close-ups of the atomized cascades and the iridescent play of rainbows. The healing power of the waterfall aerosol is scientifically proven: the forceful impact of water on rock generates an extraordinarily high concentration of negatively charged micro-droplets that penetrate deep into the lungs, demonstrably relieving asthma, allergies, and respiratory conditions (certified as a natural remedy under Krimml Hohe Tauern Health). At the valley entrance, the modern visitor centre WasserWelten Krimml showcases the phenomenon of water with an interactive exhibition and an aquapark.

Visit & Arrival

The waterfall trail is open daily during the snow-free months from mid-April to late October. A trail conservation fee is charged for path maintenance and safety infrastructure within the national park. Waterfall trail admission (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €8.00, children (aged 6 to 15) approx. €4.00; combination ticket with WasserWelten adults approx. €14.50, children approx. €7.00. Arriving by car: from Tyrol via the Zillertalstraße B169 to Zell am Ziller, continuing on the Gerlosstraße B165 over the Gerlospass to Krimml (large paid car parks P1 to P4 directly at the valley exit). By public transport: by train to Zell am Ziller or Mittersill, then by regional Postbus line directly to the bus stop Krimml Wasserfälle.

Tips

The path to the lowest waterfall tier is wide, paved, and completely barrier-free for wheelchair users and strollers; the continuation up to the middle and upper tiers climbs steeply along paved switchbacks and requires sturdy footwear with good grip. Bring a waterproof rain jacket to protect against the dense spray clouds at the viewing platforms.
